basics.name: Mateus Mendonça Monteiro
basics.label: Backend Software Engineer
basics.summary: I'm a backend software engineer. I build distributed systems and event-driven microservices for high-volume financial and retail platforms. At Itaú Unibanco I write serverless services in Python and Go, and tools that migrate data between AWS accounts and Customer Data Platforms, including mainframe sources. At LuizaLabs I worked on the search engine used by millions of people a day and cut product data synchronization time by 20%. I also do MSc research in Computer Science at UNESP, on artificial intelligence and machine learning.

work.name: Itaú Unibanco
work.summary: Build accelerator tools that migrate data between multi-account AWS environments and Customer Data Platforms (CDP). Write serverless microservices in Python and Go with hexagonal architecture, event-driven design and Data Mesh domains. Build ETL pipelines with AWS Step Functions, Glue, and Lambda. Governance and observability run on KMS, CloudTrail, CloudWatch, X-Ray, Datadog, and Grafana.
highlights: Python, Go, AWS, Step Functions, Glue, Lambda, KMS, CloudTrail, CloudWatch, X-Ray, Datadog, Grafana

work.name: LuizaLabs
work.summary: Worked on the search engine and high-throughput microservices used by millions of people a day. Stack: Java (Spring Boot, Quarkus), Node.js (Fastify), and TypeScript, backed by MongoDB, Redis, and Elasticsearch. Implemented circuit breakers and fallbacks, and cut product data synchronization time by 20% by optimizing Elasticsearch re-indexing. Built GraphQL (Apollo Federation) and REST APIs, async messaging with RabbitMQ and Pub/Sub, deployed to Kubernetes on GCP and Magalu Cloud via ArgoCD.
highlights: Java, Spring Boot, Quarkus, Node.js, Fastify, TypeScript, MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch, GraphQL, Apollo Federation, RabbitMQ, Pub/Sub, GCP, MagaluCloud, Kubernetes, ArgoCD, Datadog, Grafana

projects.name: rinha-backend-2026-c
projects.description: Fraud detection by vector search for Rinha de Backend 2026, in C11. KNN over 1,000,000 reference vectors in shared memory, with ARM Neon SIMD, 16-bit fixed-point quantization and 4,096 spatial buckets. Median latency near 250 µs on 1 vCPU and 350 MB.
highlights: Median latency near 250 µs and p95 near 430 µs under load, about 2,400 requests per second on a single worker core.
Three C binaries share memory over POSIX SHM: a loader that quantizes 1,000,000 reference vectors into 4,096 spatial buckets, HTTP workers that run KNN with k = 5, and a load balancer.
A query reads its own bucket and the nearest ones, about 8,000 records instead of 1,000,000, and stops early when the first 1,024 records give 5 identical labels.
Distances use ARM Neon SIMD on 16-bit fixed-point values, and each record is padded to 64 bytes so it sits on one cache line.

projects.name: megabrain-context-protocol
projects.description: Material for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) workshop at DevFest 2026. Builds DevBrain, an MCP server in Python that tells a coding agent whether a branch is ready for a pull request. Review rules live in code, and the same server runs in Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot and Codex.
highlights: DevBrain answers one question for a coding agent: is this branch ready for a pull request? The review rules live in code, and the agent backs its answer with what the tools returned.
The server is split into domain, application and adapters, and its tests drive it through the MCP client with no LLM in the loop.
The same server runs in Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and Codex; the repository ships a config for each host.
The student guide has the labs in class order, and the 56 slides are a reveal.js deck that opens offline. Taught with Maria Beatriz França.

projects.name: syntroph
projects.description: Go toolkit and orchestrator that connects development tools around a hexagonal core. An in-process event bus hands one adapter's output to the next, an append-only saga journal records each step, and session memory stays local, with GitHub Issues or Wiki as a mirror.
highlights: A hexagonal core with a synchronous in-process event bus: one adapter's output becomes the next adapter's input, and an append-only saga journal records each step.
Session memory is written locally under .syntroph/memory/ and mirrored to GitHub Issues or the Wiki through one explicit provider: REST, MCP or the wiki Git repository.
A remote outage never fails a local write. It becomes a pending sync, handled by the sync status, sync recovery, sync retry and sync resolve commands.
Runs with the Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity CLIs, and keeps an offline catalog of engineering skills that is published only once verified.

projects.name: transaction.ledger
projects.description: Financial order registration service on AWS serverless. Implements conditional writes for idempotency, outbox pattern with CDC, circuit breakers, and CloudWatch observability.
highlights: API Gateway with throttling (burst 20, rate 10) and a JWT Lambda authorizer in front of a FastAPI service running on AWS Lambda.
DynamoDB conditional writes on an idempotency key, so a retried request never creates a second order.
DynamoDB Streams feed an outbox Lambda that publishes the order-created event; after 3 failed attempts a message moves to an SQS dead-letter queue watched by CloudWatch alarms.
Requester validation sits behind a circuit breaker with retry, and LocalStack with WireMock reproduce the AWS setup in Docker Compose.

projects.name: codecash

projects.name: fuzzymeans-ai
projects.description: Explainable imputation of missing costs in highway-rail crossing accident records (FRA data). Fuzzy C-Means and Noise Clustering over coordinates and speeds: each imputed value is a membership-weighted mean that can be audited. Validated by masking 30% of the known values across 5 seeds.
highlights: Imputes missing damage costs in FRA highway-rail crossing accident records by clustering on latitude, longitude, train speed and vehicle speed.
Noise Clustering (Davé, 1991) adds a noise cluster at a fixed distance, so outliers such as mistyped billion-dollar damages stop pulling the real centroids.
Each imputed cost is the cluster means weighted by the accident's memberships: an equation anyone can audit.
Validation hides 30% of the known costs over 5 random seeds and compares MAE and RMSE in US dollars with mean, median, k-NN and MICE baselines. Paper and slides are in LaTeX.

projects.name: lime.stability.imputation
projects.description: MSc experimental research on LIME stability with data imputation techniques across RandomForest and GradientBoosting models.
highlights: Measures how much LIME explanations change when missing values are filled by different imputation techniques, on RandomForest and GradientBoosting models.

projects.name: find-the-fight
projects.description: Bachelor's thesis: fight detection in surveillance camera video. A classifier reads 10 frames through a pretrained Xception, passes the features to two bidirectional LSTM layers and decides between violence and non-violence; a second approach measures the distance between the centroids of each person's pose.
highlights: Each video becomes a sequence of 10 frames at 299 × 299. A frozen Xception pretrained on ImageNet extracts the features of each frame (TimeDistributed); two bidirectional LSTM layers of 64 units read the sequence, and a sigmoid output gives the probability of violence.

Trained with Adam (learning rate 0.001) and binary cross-entropy for 20 epochs. The preliminary result published at ENEPE 2022, on the Surveillance Camera Fight Dataset (300 videos, 150 with violence, 70/30 split), was 63% accuracy.
A second approach estimates poses with OpenVINO's human-pose-estimation-0001 model, takes the centroid of each skeleton and tracks the distance between people frame by frame.
Live webcam inference in a notebook, a Flask server that streams the video with AlphaPose poses, and a Streamlit prototype to upload a video. The abstract was published in the ENEPE 2022 proceedings.

highlights: Each iteration runs two sub-passes that delete boundary pixels based on their neighbourhood, until the shape is one pixel wide and still connected.
